title: MCP Resources, Prompts, and Tools
description: Learn how to model backend data and behavior using MCP resources, prompts, and tools with real examples.

blocks.text: MCP resources expose data, prompts provide reusable text templates, and tools represent callable actions. Together they let a backend present a complete AI interface: what data exists, what tasks can be performed, and how to ask for them correctly.
A resource is data that the client can read. It often maps to a database record, file, or API response. Resources are identified by a URI and can return structured content such as text or JSON.

blocks.title: MCP resource provider
blocks.content: Expose customer records as a readable resource with URI-based access.

blocks.text: A prompt is a template with named arguments. The client fills the arguments and submits the prompt to the model. Prompts are useful for standard workflows like support triage, code review, or data summarization.

blocks.title: Full MCP prompt definition
blocks.content: Prompt templates with arguments and a rendered prompt builder for the model.

blocks.text: Tools are the most powerful MCP primitive. They represent backend functions the client can execute. Each tool has a name, description, and typed input schema. Strong descriptions improve tool selection and reduce invalid arguments.

blocks.title: MCP tool with full implementation
blocks.content: A search tool with typed input schema, async execution, cancellation support, and error handling.

blocks.title: Describe tools for LLMs, not humans
blocks.text: Include examples, edge cases, and expected return formats in tool descriptions. The model reads these descriptions when choosing tools.

items.text: I can map backend concepts to MCP primitives
items.hint: Database rows to resources, reusable workflows to prompts, business logic to tools

items.text: I understand why prompt templates are useful
items.hint: They enforce structure and reduce prompt engineering drift

items.text: I know what makes a good tool description
items.hint: Clear behavior, parameter meanings, examples, and error behavior

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Resources expose data, prompts expose reusable templates, and tools expose actions.
Strong descriptions and typed schemas improve model behavior.
MCP lets you build one AI interface that works across many clients.
blocks.takeaway: Design your MCP surface from the user's goals, not from your existing database schema. The protocol is a translation layer between user intent and backend capability.
